data.rationale: Paged reads are a common source of skipped/duplicated rows; start with this small module.
Lines 35-40 of queryPages were elided in the previous output; I need the exact page-limit and termination logic before judging whether paging can drop or repeat records.
paged-read.ts looks sound: it refuses a missing cursor and a repeated one. Backups are a likely place for data loss, so read backup.ts next.
Read the backup write path and the start of the verify path. A backup that silently drops or corrupts records would be a data-loss defect.
See how the backup enumerates and reads collections (truncated in the earlier read) before checking it for missing or incomplete data.
Read the restore path to check whether it verifies record counts against the header and trailer and handles partial writes.
Backup and paged-read look careful so far. Next I'll check identity and sessions handling for expiry or race issues.
See the truncated restore lines before moving on to other modules.
Learn how existing tests construct a FeltDB state and call backup/restore, so a new test can exercise backup paths.
Find where paged reads are used, to check callers for pagination/limit defects.

Check how a mutation's find over pending writes applies limit/orderBy, a likely spot for wrong results.
Read the paged query path and the mutation overlay helpers to look for a cursor or limit defect.
Inspect the transactional query overlay path for paging/limit defects with pending writes.

See sortRecords, checkLimit, equalityWhere and asWhere, which decide what a mutation's reads return when it has pending writes.

Look for timeout/race patterns that commonly leak timers or misreport outcomes in guest execution or services.
